title: Advance Medical Directive numbers, doctor-witness rule and whether doctors may ask patients about AMDs
asked: Ms Kuah Boon Theng asked how many Advance Medical Directives (AMDs) have been registered to date, whether the requirement that an AMD always be signed before a doctor could be removed where there are no mental capacity concerns, and whether the Ministry would reassess the ban on doctors asking patients if they have an AMD.
response: As of February 2026, more than 84,500 individuals have signed an AMD. Ms Rahayu Mahzam said safeguards exist, including a witnessing doctor who checks the individual understands the medical implications, is not coerced and is of sound mind, and that strict confidentiality is maintained so knowledge of an AMD does not influence treatment decisions before terminal certification. She said operational processes ensure doctors' AMD search requests get prompt attention, including after regular office hours, and that the Ministry is reviewing the whole AMD process to increase uptake and awareness and streamline it. She added that section 15(2) of the AMD Act allows a doctor to discuss the AMD concept broadly.

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: a witnessing doctor ensures that the individual understands the medical implications of making an AMD, is not being coerced and is of sound mind

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Strict confidentiality of AMDs are maintained to ensure that the knowledge of an AMD does not inappropriately influence treatment decisions before a patient is certified terminally ill.

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We have established operational processes to ensure that AMD search requests made by doctors receive prompt attention, including after regular office hours.

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam

key_points.point: Search requests have been answered promptly, including outside office hours.

key_points.quote: there have been very prompt responses, even outside office hours, in terms of following through with a request for the search

left_open: Whether the requirement that an AMD be signed before a doctor will be removed where there are no mental capacity concerns.
Whether doctors will be permitted to ask their patients whether they have an AMD.
What the ongoing review of the AMD process will change and when it will conclude.
supplementary: Supplementary questions pressed for dropping the doctor-witness requirement and letting doctors ask patients about AMD status, citing slow uptake versus LPAs.
